qk_vs_ov_reading: mlp1 dwarfs every head by ~700x (13.37 vs max head 0.019), so the head layer is basically irrelevant here. Among heads, 6.3 is top at both grains with ov (0.0188) only ~1.7x qk (0.0112) -- same order of magnitude, so head 6.3's small contribution is mostly SELECTION (finding the right context token), not a distinctive payload. Net verdict: this well-predicted 'runners in scoring [position]' collocation is essentially entirely an mlp1 token-identity completion, not an attention circuit.
category_story: mlp1 is a giant front token-table keyed on the current token's surface identity/spelling: it fires hardest on subword/compound continuations that are near-deterministic given the current token alone -- completing a word split across BPE tokens (e.g. 'six-re'->'actor', 'epitom'->'izes', 'BRU'->'CE', 'TOGET'->'HER'), repeated legal-boilerplate compounds (e.g. 'Transferor'/'Transferee'->' spouse'), and form-filler boilerplate ('Yes___No__'->'____'). Its scope is 'the next BPE fragment of an in-progress multi-token word or fixed phrase', not context-dependent selection at all.
surprises: Expected a baseball-collocation/bigram head to show up given the sports context, but no head comes remotely close to mlp1's dCE -- mlp1 alone accounts for the position being 'well predicted'. This matches the known mlp1=giant front token-table finding directly: 'in scoring' is apparently frequent/predictable enough from token identity alone that no selection circuit is needed.
